Kātyāyanī
(‘daughter of [the sage] Kata’)
------------------------------------------
One of the forms of the Divine मोथेर्, she is so called because she was once born as the daughter of the sage Kata. She is one of the nine forms of दुर्गा (Navadurgās). Iconographical works describe her in different ways. She has three eyes and her body is bent in three places (tribhaṅga). She may be shown with four or eight or even ten arms. The objects commonly shown in her hands are: खड्ग (sword), kheṭa (shield), kamala (lotus), abhayamudrā (gesture of protection), त्रिशूल (trident), धनुस् (bow), बाण (arrow), aṅkuśa (goad), पाश (noose), शक्ति (a special weapon) परशु (battle axe) and घण्टा (bell).
A lion as her mount and the demon महिषासुर below her left foot are also shown sometimes.
In the Bhāgavata (10.22.1-5) the young girls of the cowherds are described to have performed a religious rite called ‘Kātyāyanī-vrata’ (worship of the मोथेर्-goddess कात्यायनी) in order to get कृष्ण as their husband. From this it can be surmised that कात्यायनी is an ancient folk goddess.

Kātyāyana
------------------------------------------
Kātyāyana is one of the ancient sages credited with the authorship of many works.
The Śrautasūtra of कात्यायन belongs to the Śukla Yajurveda and has 26 chapters. The yāgas described in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa are dealt with in this work in greater detail. There is a Karkabhāṣya, a commentary attributed to one Karkācārya, on this work.
Kātyāyana is also the author of a Śulbasūtra with seven kaṇḍikās or sections. It deals mainly with the construction of the vedis or platforms for the performance of वेदिच् सच्रिड़िचेस्. The knowledge of geometry revealed in this work is astonishing.
Two more works on the वेदस्, attributed to कात्यायन are available now: Sarvānukramaṇī on the Ṛgveda and a similar work on the Śukla Yajurveda.
Many authors of धर्मशास्त्रस् like शङ्ख-लिखित, याज्ञवल्क्य and पराशर have considered कात्यायन as an important expounder of धर्म.
Though his original work on the various aspects of धर्म is not available now, numerous quotations from his work are seen in the निबन्धस् or digests by other authors.
One Kātyāyanasmṛti, also called Karmapradīpa, available now is in three prapāṭhakas (sections) divided into 29 khaṇḍas (chapters) and has 500 verses. This work contains miscellaneous topics like wearing of sacred thread, worship of deities like गणेश and the Mātṛkās, details of some implements useful in वेदिच् सच्रिड़िचेस्, personal hygiene, सन्ध्या ritual, the five daily sacrifices, śrāddha and so on.
The date of कात्यायन has been approximately placed between the 4th and the 6th centuries A. D.
There is another कात्यायन (a grammarian), the author of vārttikās or critical explanatory and complementary notes on certain rules of पाणिनि’s Sanskrit grammar. पतञ्जलि (200 B. C.), the composer of the Mahābhāṣya on पाणिनि’s Aṣṭādhyāyī often quotes his vārttikas.
